en.name: Vegetable juice, homemade
en.summary: Homemade vegetable juice keeps 3–5 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. It is raw and unpasteurised and, unlike citrus, it has almost no acidity to protect it — so it is not advised for young children, older adults, pregnant women or anyone with a weakened immune system.
en.pantry: There is no room-temperature timeline for homemade vegetable juice, and there should not be one. Juicing releases everything inside the vegetable into a liquid that is low in acid, rich in sugars and minerals and still carrying whatever was on the skins and in the juicer. Between 4 °C and 60 °C that liquid is in the danger zone. Apply the two-hour rule strictly — one hour if the room is above 32 °C — and get the juice into the fridge the moment it is made.
en.fridge: 3–5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in a clean, tightly closed bottle filled as full as you can, on a shelf rather than in the door. Wash the vegetables properly before juicing and scrub anything that grew in soil, because the juicer will carry whatever is on the skin straight into the bottle. Clean the juicer immediately after use for the same reason. Expect separation and settling — shake before pouring — and pour into a glass rather than drinking from the bottle.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for homemade vegetable juice. Freezing works and is a reasonable way to handle a glut from the garden, especially if the juice is destined for soups and sauces rather than for drinking; leave headspace because the liquid expands, and freeze in single portions. Thawed juice separates and tastes duller, which matters less in a pan than in a glass.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, never on the counter, then shake or blend. Treat thawed juice as freshly made again and drink it within the refrigerated window.
spoilage: A sour, yeasty or fermented smell instead of a fresh, earthy one.
A thick, slimy or ropey texture.
Mould at the neck of the bottle or floating on the surface.
tips: Wash and scrub the vegetables before juicing; the juicer transfers everything on the skin.
Clean the juicer straight after use, especially the mesh basket.
Fill the bottle to the top so there is as little air above the juice as possible.
Add lemon or lime — a little acid improves both the flavour and the keeping.

faq.q: How long does homemade vegetable juice last?
faq.a: 3–5 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in a clean closed bottle.
It is raw and low in acid, so it carries a real risk of foodborne illness and is not advised for young children, older adults, pregnant women or anyone immunocompromised.

faq.q: Can you freeze homemade vegetable juice?
faq.a: No freezer timeline is published, but it works in practice. Leave headspace, freeze in portions, and use thawed juice in cooking where the separation matters less.

zh.name: 自製蔬菜汁
zh.summary: 自製蔬菜汁放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 3～5 天。它是生的、未殺菌的，而且和柑橘不同，它幾乎沒有酸度可以保護自己——所以不建議幼兒、年長者、孕婦或免疫力較弱的人飲用。
zh.pantry: 自製蔬菜汁沒有室溫的期限，也不該有。榨汁把蔬菜裡的一切都釋放進一杯低酸、富含糖分與礦物質的液體裡，而那杯液體仍然帶著蔬菜表皮與榨汁機上原有的一切。在 4 °C 到 60 °C 之間，它就在危險溫度帶裡。請嚴格套用兩小時原則——室溫超過 32 °C 時只有一小時——並且榨好立刻送進冰箱。
zh.fridge: 用乾淨、蓋緊、盡量裝滿的瓶子，放 4 °C 以下、冰箱層架（不是門邊），3～5 天。榨之前請把蔬菜洗乾淨，土裡長出來的要刷洗，因為榨汁機會把表皮上的一切原封不動送進瓶子裡。用完立刻清洗榨汁機，理由相同。它會分層沉澱——倒之前搖一搖——而且請倒進杯子喝，不要對瓶口喝。
zh.freezer: 自製蔬菜汁沒有公布的冷凍期限。冷凍可行，自家菜園一次收太多時也是合理的處理方式，尤其如果這些汁本來就要拿去做湯或醬汁；請留膨脹空間，並分成單次份量。解凍後會分層、味道也變鈍，但在鍋子裡沒有在杯子裡那麼要緊。
zh.thawing: 請放冷藏解凍，不要放檯面上，之後搖勻或重新打勻。解凍後就當成剛做好的，在冷藏的期限內喝完。
spoilage: 聞起來酸、有酵母味或發酵味，而不是清新的泥土香。
質地變得濃稠、黏滑或牽絲。
tips: 榨之前把蔬菜洗淨刷乾淨；榨汁機會把表皮上的東西全部帶過去。
用完立刻清洗榨汁機，尤其是濾網。
瓶子裝滿到頂，讓汁液上方的空氣越少越好。
加點檸檬或萊姆；一點酸度對風味和保存都有幫助。

faq.q: 自製蔬菜汁可以放多久？
faq.a: 用乾淨密封的瓶子放 4 °C 以下冷藏 3～5 天。
它是生的、酸度又低，確實帶有食因性疾病的風險，不建議幼兒、年長者、孕婦或免疫力較弱的人飲用。

faq.q: 自製蔬菜汁可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 沒有公布的冷凍期限，但實務上可行。請留膨脹空間、分裝，解凍後拿去入菜，分層就沒那麼要緊。
